title: Bound the k=76 caller with a degree-three exceptional HOST
body:
The specified degree-three exceptional HOST branch has normalized actual invoice at most 24488606814627813/190000000000000, below 128.887404287515 and the 128.891 bar. This includes the maximum allowed one-IDLE correction.

## Scope and source

Requires k=76, Q=T=1, the stated P=−I signed frame and named global event assignment with exceptional HOST on {e,s,t}. The pair kernel forces 73 pairs onto the other 72 nonhub roles. The source extension is #7869 at `06c207a9feb3994a4b987dc3010657b6e85b7956`. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`. The included source manifest identifies every public dependency used.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-near-hub-degree-three/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory, check its checksum manifest, and run the extracted commands. The original and separate 72-role integer-root DP checks passed along with the source and accounting controls. Both legal residual partitions were evaluated. Hosted execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Prove the named global assignment and related legal-word bridge, or bound other exceptional HOST role sizes.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. [Campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
